issue.title: Artifact links whose target is a bead never reach the bead: _upsert_bead only inspects source_ref
issue.description:
`sase artifact link add <non-bead> <relation> bead:<id>` stores the row on the source
artifact only. The bead gets no `link_added` event and no row on its generated page, so
the edge is invisible from the bead side.

Reproduced on 2026-08-24 at `cbea4f23b`:

```bash
sase artifact link add research:202608/artifact_link_adoption.md related bead:sase-r8 "..."
sase artifact link list research:202608/artifact_link_adoption.md   # row present
grep -c link_added sase/repos/beads/events/streams/sase-r8.jsonl    # 0
```

The row lands in `research/links/202608/artifact_link_adoption.md.json` and in the
project aggregate, but `sase-r8`'s event stream gained nothing and its page has no Links
block.

Root cause, `src/sase/sdd/_artifact_link_store_impl.py:382` in `_upsert_bead`:

```python
issue_id = bead_id_from_ref(str(incoming["source_ref"]))
if issue_id is None:
    return None
```

Only `source_ref` is inspected. A bead in the target position is skipped entirely.
Corroborated against the corpus: all 26 `link_added` events in the store have a bead as
source (23 -> `bead`, 3 -> `plan`); not one was written by an inbound edge.

Impact is worst for `related`, which the relation registry declares undirected
(`inverse: related, directed: no`) - an undirected edge stored on one endpoint only is
half an edge. It also splits consumers: the ACE beads pane reads the aggregate and shows
the edge, while `sase bead show` and the generated bead page read the event stream and do
not. Any future `plan implements bead:<id>` derivation lands on the plan and is invisible
from the bead, which is the direction someone browsing beads actually wants.

Fix: `_upsert_bead` should write an endpoint event for a bead in **either** position,
storing the registry-declared inverse relation when the bead is the target. Backfill the
endpoint events the current one-sided writes never produced.

task_type_fields.repro:
Reproduced at `cbea4f23b`, 2026-08-24:

```bash
sase artifact link add research:202608/artifact_link_adoption.md related bead:sase-r8 "why"
sase artifact link list research:202608/artifact_link_adoption.md   # row is present
grep -c link_added "$(sase repo path beads)/events/streams/sase-r8.jsonl"   # prints 0
```

The row is written to `research/links/202608/artifact_link_adoption.md.json` and to the
project aggregate; the bead's event stream and generated page get nothing.

Corpus check - every existing bead link event has the bead as source:

```bash
sase artifact link list -j -l 0 | python3 -c "import json,sys; r=json.load(sys.stdin); print([x['relation'] for x in r if x['target_ref'].startswith('bead:') and not x['source_ref'].startswith('bead:')])"
```

payload.entry: Stale-bead sweep 2026-08-27 (project owner asked for a review of every open task bead in sase and bob-cli). Verified at master eaf4ea891 in workspace sase_15 after just install. _upsert_bead moved to src/sase/sdd/_artifact_link_store_bead_rows.py:28 and now resolves both endpoints: source_issue_id = bead_id_from_ref(source_ref) and target_issue_id = bead_id_from_ref(target_ref), appending an add_bead_endpoint_link write for each with direction 'out'/'in'. The bead-as-target skip described in this bead's root-cause section is gone. Commit e391b1a28 ('feat(artifact-links): derive plan implements-key and backfill sweep') also added the backfill this bead asked for.

payload.close_reason: Fixed: _upsert_bead now writes an endpoint event for a bead in either position, and the backfill sweep for the one-sided history shipped with it.
